newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start with big jump, then retrace.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start with big jump, then retrace.

text.p: French shares started higher, supported by gains in bonds and a steady dollar, traders said. A firmer close on Wall Street also helped sentiment.
But business remained quiet as investors, particularly foreign funds, stayed on the sidelines, awaiting results of the British and French parliamentary elections.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 9.68 points or 0.38 percent at 2,559.93 at 0827 GMT, after opening up 0.82 percent.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 1.5 at 2,556.5 from Monday's close.
Volume was 390 million francs.
* Bouygues rises 2.63 percent to 546 after positive analysts' meeting yesterday. A broker said the stock was considered cheap on a net asset value estimated at 750 francs per share.
Broker Oddo, which held its overweight recommendation, expects future earnings to be largely made up of exceptionals.

* Blue chip Alcatel Alsthom gains 0.96 percent to 629, among the highest turnover stocks. Chairman Serge Tchuruk said in an interview with Le Figaro newspaper that privatisation of Thomson-CSF should not be delayed as the sell-off is vital to European defence restructuring.
* Thomson-CSF was up 0.45 percent at 177 francs.

* SEB gains 2.79 percent to 1,030 after Monday's analysts meeting. The acquisition of Arno of Brazil is expected to be earnings positive by 32 million francs this year, or adding 2.2 francs per share, and by 43 million, or 2.8 francs per share, in 1998.
Oddo revised upward estimates to 38.8 francs per share in 1997 versus 36.6 previously, and to 44.6 from 41.8 for 1998.
* Euro Disney EDLPA falls 1.52 percent to 9.75 francs. First half losses of 210 million were in line with forecasts.
A broker said the theme park operator had been expected to post losses in the first half as it is the low season and even with gains on the operating line.
* Among U.S. indicators due today are first quarter employment costs and durable goods.
* The London FTSE index was at its highest level for six weeks after breaking through 4,400, just two days before a parliamentary eelction in which polls put the New Labour as favoured to win.
* France votes in a two round parliamentary elections on May 25 and June 1. Opinion polls put the centre-right RPR-UDF ahead of the Socialist party with a reduced but clear majority.
The market expects to rally strongly if the RPR-UDF coalition returns to power with a fresh mandate for pursuing European monetary union and rolling back the public sector.
* Insurer GAN was down 6.62 percent at 141 francs, after reporting a 1996 loss of 5.7 billion francs.
* INSEE statistics showed flat consumer spending for March after a 1.3 percent fall in February.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
